newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 oil pool gap seen at 155 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 oil pool gap seen at 155 bln rupees.

text.p: India's oil pool deficit, which is the amount reimbursed by the government to oil companies to make up for subsidised prices, is expected at 155 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) against 57 billion rupees in 1995/96, Petroleum Minister T.R. Baalu said on Wednesday.
"The oil pool deficit will be 155 billion rupees by 31 March, 1997," Baalu told a business editors' conference in the Indian capital.
Petroleum Ministry officials said the oil pool deficit was expected to grow steeply following an increase in international crude oil prices.
"The correction of the oil pool deficit is the cumulative responsibility of the cabinet, Baalu said.

Economic analysts say the government faces a challenge in curtailing expenditure on account of the deficit, which is a cumulative outstanding amount owed by the government to state-run petroleum companies.

"The depreciation of the value of the rupee, increased imports, rise in international prices and the non-adjustment of selling prices to the required extent have pushed the cumulative outstanding claims of the oil companies..," Baalu said.
"This is likely to create serious problems in procurement and supplies as well as completion of projects," he said.
The government partially rolled back a petroleum product price hike effected earlier this year after protests from the political opposition.
